gloss: stationing; being posted (abroad or at a location)

definitions.gloss: stationing; being posted; residing for duty
definitions.explanation: Being assigned to live and work at a particular location, especially overseas, for work purposes. Commonly used for diplomats, company employees on overseas assignments, and police officers assigned to local posts.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{三年間|さんねんかん}アメリカに{駐在|ちゅうざい}していた。
examples.english: My father was posted in America for three years.

examples.japanese: {駐在|ちゅうざい}さんが{毎朝|まいあさ}{通学路|つうがくろ}に{立|た}っている。
examples.english: The local police officer stands along the school route every morning.
examples.notes: 駐在さん is a colloquial way to refer to a resident police officer.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}からシンガポールに{駐在|ちゅうざい}することになり、{家族|かぞく}で{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}す{準備|じゅんび}をしている。
examples.english: I'll be posted to Singapore starting next month, so we're preparing for the family to move.

notes:
USAGE:
Very common in business contexts for overseas assignments. A {駐在員|ちゅうざいいん} (expatriate employee) is someone posted abroad by their company. In rural Japan, {駐在|ちゅうざい}さん refers to the local resident police officer stationed at a small police box ({駐在所|ちゅうざいしょ}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駐在員|ちゅうざいいん} (expatriate employee; stationed worker)
- {駐在所|ちゅうざいしょ} (residential police box)
- {海外|かいがい}{駐在|ちゅうざい} (overseas posting)
- {駐在|ちゅうざい}{妻|づま} (expat wife)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {赴任|ふにん}: taking up a post — focuses on the act of going to a new assignment
- {常駐|じょうちゅう}: permanent stationing — being stationed full-time at a client site or location
